The non-delivery is phrased conditionally, but the substance is covered.

Issue 2 identifies the 100% sale as a Change of Control under §1.3 requiring consent under §14.2, with a termination right under §14.3. It notes the consent is omitted from Schedule 3.6 and so from §6.4 and §7.1(d). It recommends adding the consent to Schedule 3.6 and seeking it immediately.

Issue 4 identifies the six-state versus four-state mismatch, the post-term restricted period, and recommends narrowing the Side Letter territory. It never explains that the Side Letter's expanded Territory definition controls under the §19.4 order-of-precedence clause. §19.4 is cited only in Issue 5, on governing law.

Issue 5 identifies New York law and New York County jurisdiction against Delaware §18.1/§18.2. It explains the conflict and the risk of differing analysis by the two states' courts. It recommends a conforming amendment to align governing law and forum, though it does not expressly say to conform to Delaware.
